  • According to recent reports, new to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

According to recent reports, new to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

This option is right now rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

In a recent development, try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a latest thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills.

Sources indicate that certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

In a recent development, are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google states:.

“Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google mentioned on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

Recent findings suggest that google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

For those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

It has been revealed that chatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

Recent findings suggest that I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. On Tuesday, Google announced that it would be rolling out latest settings through which you could opt out of AI model training without losing access to your chat history.

#1887. UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (746 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

UK court rules Apple can share the top secret order everyone already knew

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (746 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.
  • Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the matter ….
  • In a recent development, the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the matter ….

In a recent development, the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

The feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

Sources indicate that in 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

This would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve said many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

It would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the firm found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple announced it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

“Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to new consumers and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have said many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

At this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

According to recent reports, the iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

The UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal stated. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it debuted – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

This ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

Linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

So too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this upcoming take on the OS is the epitome of that.

In a recent development, the distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with new ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

It has been revealed that the developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

If you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

In a recent development, pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

Sources indicate that at the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a new workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

Sources indicate that pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

According to recent reports, another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

Once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

According to recent reports, as I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One concern that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI upgrade system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

Sources indicate that I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an revision component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

It would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

It has been revealed that you should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my new favorite free productivity suite.

Pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

Breaking: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (730 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Blog

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tool Retrieval is now in preview in the Gemini Interactions API.
  • We are launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API to help your agents manage large tool libraries more efficiently.
  • In a recent development, we are introducing Tool Retrieval to help developers manage large collections of software tools more efficiently.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tool Retrieval is now in preview in the Gemini Interactions API. Load tool parameter schemas on demand instead of sending your full tool library in every prompt,designed to reduce input tokens and keep tool selection accurate as your agent scales.

Research Scientist, Google DeepMind.

Your browser does not support the audio element.

We are launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API to help your agents manage large tool libraries more efficiently. By loading parameter schemas only when needed, you reduce latency and input token costs for complex tasks. You can try this feature today in the Interactions API by adding a tool_search tool and setting defer_loading to true in your requests.

In a recent development, we are introducing Tool Retrieval to help developers manage large collections of software tools more efficiently. Instead of loading every tool at once, your agent now keeps a library on standby and only pulls in the specific details it needs for a task. This reduces data usage, speeds up performance, and improves accuracy. You can start using this feature today with our latest Gemini models to build more capable and responsive applications.

Today we're launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, available in preview in the Interactions API.

Sources indicate that when an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools, sending every full parameter schema on every request adds up fast. It inflates input token counts, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows. Tool Retrieval lets your agent keep its full tool library on standby and load parameter schemas only when the current task needs them.

To turn on Tool Retrieval, add a tool_search tool to your request and set defer_loading: true on the tools you want to hold back. The model still sees the name and description of every deferred tool, so it knows what's available, but the parameter schemas stay out of context. When the model needs a tool, it asks for it by name, the API loads the full schema, and the model calls the function, all inside the same request.

Inside that single API call, the model searches for issue_refund, the API loads its schema, and the model emits the function_call. All three steps appear in interaction.steps, making it easy to inspect which tools the model considered when debugging tool names or descriptions:.

From here it's normal function calling: your code runs the refund and sends back a function_result.

In a recent development, there's no index to build or host. Gemini runs the search on the server, so the only changes to your code are the fresh tool and a flag on the tools you want to defer. You can keep your most-used tools loaded up front and defer the long tail.

In a recent development, tool Retrieval also plays well with prefix caching. Deferred schemas stay out of the start of the prompt, and the schemas the model loads are added later in the conversation, so the cached prefix stays the same from turn to turn.

Tool Retrieval also works with remote MCP servers in the Gemini API. Set defer_loading: true on an mcp_server tool and every tool that server exposes is loaded on demand, so you can connect a large server without listing its tools one by one.

Industry observers note that if you maintain your own tool registry, embedding index, or per-user permission filter, declare the tool_search with "execution": "client" and define your search parameters. Client-side retrieval adds one round trip per search, because your app runs the lookup. Tools do not need to be declared upfront, so you can also expose fresh tools mid-conversation when a user connects an integration:.

Industry observers note that tool Retrieval has no separate charge. Input and output tokens are billed at the standard rates for the model you call. Turning on tool_search adds a small, fixed block of input tokens, and each schema the model loads is billed as input for the rest of the conversation, the same as a tool declared up front. You save tokens when the schemas you never load outweigh the ones you do, which is the usual case for large libraries. Measure it against your own traffic.

Tool Retrieval works with Gemini 3.6 and later models, including all Gemini 4 models, in the Interactions API.

#1882. Simon Jack: Can Anthropic's record-breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?

Simon Jack: Can Anthropic's record-breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1616 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It was during November 2020 that somewhere in San Francisco, a woman called Daniela Amodei phoned a friend, asking for advice.
  • Daniela oversaw safety and policy at OpenAI, one of the most talked-about AI companies in the world.
  • But Daniela and her brother Dario - who worked there too - had misgivings over safety levels at OpenAI and thought it could be time to walk away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was during November 2020 that somewhere in San Francisco, a woman called Daniela Amodei phoned a friend, asking for advice.

Daniela oversaw safety and policy at OpenAI, one of the most talked-about AI companies in the world.

But Daniela and her brother Dario - who worked there too - had misgivings over safety levels at OpenAI and thought it could be time to walk away.

So she did what many do when we can't make a decision about something, she phoned a friend. The friend's reply was direct and to the point: "You don't need to be on the phone with me. You already know the answer.".

In a recent development, the Amodei siblings and a handful of other colleagues quit. Together, they set up a rival â Anthropic.

Six years on and Anthropic, the maker of leading AI model Claude, has predicted revenues of $52bn in 2026 and $135bn in 2027, according to analyst estimates.

It is selling shares to the public for the first time in what's known as an Initial Public Offering or IPO, aiming for a valuation of an estimated $1.4tn (Â£1tn), which would propel it straight into the top 10 of the most valuable US companies.

The sale comes at a crucial time when many are wondering whether, amid increasing concern about the potential of AI, the industry's bubble is showing signs of bursting.

Where once investors were "all in" on a technological revolution to rival the railroads, the car, electricity and the internet, some are now hedging their bets, amid arguments that AI prices will be driven down as the technology becomes more common and concerns that a hefty wedge of the AI investment is tech giants investing in each other.

Shares in companies that supply the raw computing power behind AI, like Coreweave and Nebius, have seen their value cut in half while even the mighty Nvidia has lost its crown as the world's most valuable tech giant with its shares down 30% - a staggering $2tn fall in value.

So could the Anthropic IPO reinflate the bubble or will it be remembered as the last gasp of a boom that is heading for a bust?

At an event last week, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told JPMorgan Chase's CEO Jamie Dimon that his guiding principle was to "never let your firm be worth a single dollar more than it's worth".

According to recent reports, the company is selling roughly $81bn worth of shares to the general public and a further $26bn on to other big tech companies. It is comfortably the single biggest money raising event in US corporate history.

âDaniela Amodei: The price of AIâ.

Sources indicate that it's an old adage that during a gold rush you should buy companies that sell the picks and shovels as opposed to those staking everything on striking gold. In AI's case that's the chip makers, the data centre builders, the energy providers. But Anthropic is arguably the gold itself and this IPO will see what value people put on it, according to Fiona Cincotta from StoneX trading.

Industry observers note that "I think the reason that this IPO is so important is basically it's the first ability for the public investors to access a pure play AI trade," she notes, adding that previous offerings have been about "other parts of the ecosystem, which are, the semiconductors, the chips, the, data centres. But this is the first time that we were actually able to access the AI provider.".

Daniela Amodei helped set up a rival company to OpenAI.

What a manufacturer is worth depends almost entirely on predicted future earnings.

It's that calculation that many think presents the sharpest needle to the AI bubble.

Will current and future customers of AI be prepared to pay enough to justify the trillions being spent on the chips, data centres, energy and employees, some of whom can command annual salaries of over $100m?

Recent findings suggest that "AI is certainly in a financial bubble. While LLMs [large language models] offer genuine utility and are undoubtedly here to stay, the economics don't add up," mentioned Gary Marcus, Professor Emeritus at Newly introduced York University and author of Taming Silicon Valley, speaking earlier this year.

"[The] more companies build AI models, the [more the] technology becomes commoditised, eliminating meaningful competitive advantages and driving down prices.".

So far, the growth rates in Anthropic revenue are extraordinary.

But these explosive growth rates hide a potential problem. Around a quarter of that revenue came from just a handful of companies, among them Google and Amazon.

It's also concentrated in the US which accounts for two-thirds of its revenue.

According to recent reports, there is also the staggering network of circular financing found in the AI world. For example, Anthropic has agreements to buy or lease hundreds of billions of dollars worth of chips and computing power from a handful of companies including Broadcom, Google, Amazon. Many of those firms are also investors in Anthropic and major customers of its products.

Recent findings suggest that it's not just some Wall Street investors questioning whether the AI boom is all it's cracked up to be. Out on Main Street, ordinary Americans have concerns too.

With the US driving so much of global AI growth, a growing public backlash against a technology that threatens to replace millions of jobs and hoover up vast amounts of energy and water became a factor in the recent midterm elections in the US.

Recent findings suggest that many areas in the US have passed moratoriums on data centre development and many candidates deemed too close to substantial tech found that association a political liability rather than an asset. Many Democrat candidates publicly opposed data centre development and won.

Added to that, the Pied Piper of AI, chip maker Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, resigned last week after admitting to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang and another with a company executive who reported to him.

Dario Amodei is one of Silicon Valley's major beasts.

Huang's spectacular fall from grace and Nvidia's 30% fall in value from its peak have left AI investors looking for a new champion for the AI boom that has underpinned the US stock market and arguably much of its entire economy for the last two years.

If Anthropic and its CEO are to be AI's fresh Pied Piper, he will be playing a different tune to the relentlessly upbeat, leather jacket-clad talisman Huang.

While Huang wanted AI development to continue full throttle, Anthropic was built on misgivings over the levels of safety and responsibility the OpenAI leavers felt were being exercised over the development of society-changing technology.

Amodei has warned that AI capabilities could enable biological weapon development, mass surveillance, authoritarianism and the replacement of millions of white-collar, tax-paying workers.

He has called for a slowdown in its development as its powers are growing at such an exponential rate that it could very soon elude any human oversight.

That said, his paternalistic overtures have been sceptically received by those who point out that the pace of Anthropic's development of new more powerful models has shown no sign of the slowdown he's advocating for the rest of the industry.

But for all the concerns, just as with Elon Musk's SpaceX before it, the hype and the FOMO (fear of missing out) on an undoubtedly profound moment in technological and perhaps human development, means that buying interest is high.

It's reported that orders to buy shares exceed the number on offer by over six times.

With demand outstripping supply by such a margin, a first-day jump is to be expected given the oversubscription, but it doesn't tell you much about long-run return.

Using SpaceX as an example again, shares initially rose nearly 70% from its IPO sale price of $135 to $225. Shares in SpaceX are currently back to $145.

The Anthropic IPO could be wildly successful and blow a bit of fresh fresh air into what some maintain still looks a lot like a bubble.

Eileen Burbidge, founder of tech investors Passion Capital, is one of those who reject the notion that AI is a bubble about to burst.

It has been revealed that "Maybe the growth of the bubble has slowed down a little bit, but actually I wouldn't be willing to say that it's about to burst yet," claims Burbidge. "I think this IPO could actually mean everyone could be off to the races again.".

Fiona Cincotta believes Anthropic's IPO is about far more than just Anthropic. "I think what's going to be really interesting here is I think it can actually be used as a valuation benchmark for the entire AI ecosystem," she says.

Industry observers note that "That's why I don't think this is just going to affect the share price of Anthropic. I think this is going to have much wider implications across the whole AI trade.".

Recent findings suggest that two things can be true at the same time. The Anthropic IPO could be wildly successful - FOMO is a powerful emotion in financial markets. But its probable success won't soothe the unease in some quarters that not every company, every investor and every citizen will think of AI as the answer to humanity's problems.

Yesterday Apple released its first post-launch software update for HomeView, less than a week after the product debuted.

Per the manufacturer’s official release notes, HomeView 27.2.1 focuses on bug fixes, including a fix for the following glitch:.

Pairing with an iPhone or iPad running the iOS or iPadOS 27.3 beta may cause Siri requests to fail.

Sources indicate that if you’re on iOS 27.3, Siri on HomeView can’t use your iPhone for personal context, likely until December.HomeView won’t send Siri requests to an iPhone on newer software. Without a HomeView patch, your only option is iOS 27.2.x.On-device requests like timers still work. https://t.co/8UbRs7z496.

It’s understandable that complications might arise from having iOS and HomeView software that’s out of sync. Unfortunately though, there’s no beta software available for HomeView at the moment.

That means unless Apple releases a beta soon, owners might have to wait until the public launch of HomeView 27.3 in December to get Personal Content features back.

Not since the release of 2014's Level Over headphones has Samsung stepped into the world of over-ear audio devices, and more leaks of its upcoming 'Galaxy Studio' headphones bring us one step closer to its potential unveiling.

We came across a wave of leaks back in October, where we first heard news that Samsung could challenge Sony and Apple with its own flagship headphones, but thanks to the eagle-eyed experts at SammyGuru, we now have illustrations and visual components that showcase the Galaxy Studio's versatile functions.

From what we know so far, design-wise, the Galaxy Studio headphones come in two shades (black or beige), with collapsible ear pads for travelling. The headphones are also projected to have an 870mAh battery.

Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy Studio headphones have a flexible design. - Samsung is developing high-end Galaxy Studio wireless headphones that may launch with the Galaxy S27 series early next year. - FCC documents suggest the headphones have flexible earcups that fold flat for easier storage and carrying. - They support Bluetooth and Bluetooth LE, will come in Beige and Black, and would be Samsung’s first wireless headphones in over a decade. Visit our website for more in-depth information about this and other Samsung-related news. Source: FCCNovember 5, 2026.

The reigning champion of our best wireless headphones, the Sony WH-1000 XM6 model, has clearly been an influence on the Galaxy Studio's development, but Samsung has also added its own flair to the device.

Just like its competitor, the Galaxy Studio packs most of its controls on the right ear pad. This supports touch gestures that trigger a multitude of functions, including tap to pause and play, double-tap to skip songs, triple-tap to go back, and there's even a touch-and-hold gesture that introduces an AI assistant. It's pretty standard stuff for headphones, but the AI assistant integration gives it an extra boost.

Industry observers note that as for its audio tools, it's more or less the same story. According to the animations leaked from the outlet, the Galaxy Studio has both Active Noise Canceling (ANC) and Ambient sound modes, with additional controls for ANC level, Ambient sound volume, and noise control level.

Just like Sony's range of over-ear headphones, it's likely that the Galaxy Studio will pack head tracking support, allowing spatial audio to adjust as you move your head. The headphones are expected to have an auto power-off tool where, if no audio is playing, the device turns off after a set period of time. In the APK, Samsung lists options for 30-minute, 60-minute, or 120-minute timeframe settings.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

On top of this, the left ear pad will sport volume buttons, which Sony's flagship headphones don't have. Instead, you can adjust audio volume by vertically swiping up or down on the left ear pad.

It has been revealed that new leak demonstrates Samsung's upcoming wireless headphones, the Galaxy Studio, is a solid AirPods Max and Sony WH-1000XM6 rival - Samsung’s Galaxy Studio headphones reportedly pack an 870mAh battery, USB-C charging, and wired audio playback support. - The leak claims they include ANC, ambient sound controls, wear detection, touch gestures, and AI assistant support. - Other features mentioned are 360 Audio with head tracking, Buds Auto Switch, Auracast, Samsung Find, and support for SSC UHQ and LC3 codecs. Visit our website for more in-depth information about this and other Samsung-related news. Source: SammyGuruNovember 19, 2026.

As mentioned, the Galaxy Studio model will mark Samsung's first over-ear headphones release in 12 years, and between then and now, the audio game has changed drastically across the board among tech giants.

Of course, Samsung needs to take a couple of pages from the books of its rivals to play catch-up, but it's also focused on developing its own flagship features — most notably its versatile connectivity.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to its audio functions, the leaks point to two separate ports (USB-C and 3.5mm), which allow you to connect the Galaxy Studio headphones to a mobile device for wired listening. This is a connectivity feature that Sony has yet to integrate into its own audio hardware lineup.

Listening wirelessly via Bluetooth is convenient, but true audiophiles know that wired listening is the best way to bring out the lossless and hi-res quality of digital music streaming. That mentioned, the leaks don't detail how much the Galaxy Studio headphones reduce latency, the USB audio bit depth, or sample rate, so it'll take a series of hands-on experiences to determine how the headphones perform in that department.

In a recent development, the most frustrating part is that, at the end of the day, the headphones are still in development, so whether or not some of these specs make it into the final product is another story. But if everything lines up according to what we've seen so far, I fear that Sony, Apple, and Bose alike will start shaking in their boots.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations.
  • Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.
  • According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse stated the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations. Even Meta employees are reporting concerning incidents, including the agent taking actions they didn’t ask it to and sharing information they didn’t recognize that appears to belong to other people.

Also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse stated the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing owners’ private data,” Reuters said.

Reuters said “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she stated she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

Similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

Recent findings suggest that these are just the latest in a string of alarming incidents surrounding Muse. In its first month, a cybersecurity professional discovered Muse had a serious zero-day bug that made it hijackable. At least one journalist found the AI sifting through his Apple Messages after he’d explicitly denied those permissions, which Apple then issued stronger privacy protections to address. Banks have also blocked agents over concerns.

Industry observers note that as a firm, Meta doesn’t have a solid history of respecting user privacy. That legacy is partly what informed ZDNET contributor David Gewirtz’s suspicion of the AI assistant when he tested it, though it earned his assigned title of “worst AI agent for privacy” all on its own. The agent asked him for everything from contacts and chats to his logins and passwords, and Meta automatically uses conversations with Muse to train its AI.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

Public awareness of the risks of AI agents hit a peak last year with the viral OpenClaw. The predominant advice for using agents has been to take every privacy precaution: Be careful with the data you share and the apps you give it permissions for, and watch what you tell it. But if users believe they’re doing so by restricting access to certain apps, just for Muse to find a way in anyway, privacy hygiene isn’t enough.

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible.

Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what owners need to know.

The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

In a recent development, “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

On the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly says it has no plans for a native Mac app.

You can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft plans to offer an export option before the apps retire.

Recent findings suggest that planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the organization.

Sources indicate that the June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the organization behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

Does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

After years of anticipation and delays, as well as controversy around worker rights, Grand Theft Auto 6 has completed its phased worldwide release and is available to gamers everywhere, including the UK.

There has been near universal praise from critics, with review aggregator Metacritic calculating its average score at 99 out of 100 based on 150 reviews., external.

Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has held the top spot since 1998 - but Metacritic confirmed to the BBC that this has now officially been overtaken.

GTA 6 is set to become one of the world's most popular entertainment products ever, with fans booking time off work, and schools warning students not to bunk off.

Some schools have reminded parents and pupils to prioritise study over the game, which has an 18 rating, external for "strong graphic violence, strong sexual themes and use of illegal drugs".

One school in Essex incentivised pupils to attend with prizes such as vouchers, Christmas dinners and a pass to skip the lunch queue.

According to recent reports, the UK rating means it can only be legally sold to an adult. It does not stop an adult letting their child play the game - instead it is meant to inform their decision.

It's the game that shocked and thrilled the world: Grand Theft Auto. As a new installment is released in 2026, go deep into the history of the game with rapper Bugzy Malone.

The game, set in the fictional US state of Leonida, follows two protagonists, Lucia and Jason, through the seedy underbelly of America after an "easy score goes wrong".

It was released at midnight in all the countries it is available in, which meant Latest Zealanders were the first to access it.

Recent findings suggest that "The graphics are great. Even from the set-up and credits, it's feeling pretty good," Aleana Fernando, who lives in Auckland, New Zealand, told BBC Newsbeat soon after she started playing.

Once the game was released at midnight UK time, gamers were equally enthralled by the game's graphics and attention to detail.

Charlie Wood from London said he had "already laughed at the dialogue before even stepping into the gameplay".

About 30 minutes into playing in Leonida, he mentioned it was "most definitely worth the wait".

Meanwhile in Germany, Timur told the BBC he was impressed by how lifelike the game was.

"It really feels like a life simulation with the amount of in-game encounters," he remarked.

The Guardian's Keza MacDonald, external was impressed by the relationship between the main characters.

"GTA has never been particularly kind to women... there is still a lot of sexism in GTA VI's world, but now we have Lucia to react to it," she said.

"This is the first GTA in which I have felt the women are treated as people, not only Lucia but also the many other female characters in the story".

From the memes to the music - from the controversies to the culture - you have your say on GTA 6 with Newsbeat's Jordan Kenny and De-Graft Mensah.

After GTA 5 became one of the most successful entertainment products of all time - with estimates of net profits soaring as high up as $10bn (Â£7.6bn) - anticipation could not be higher for the sixth instalment.

Makers Rockstar North, headquartered in Edinburgh, delayed the release twice, saying it needed extra months to finish the game with the level of polish fans had come to "expect and deserve".

The company was also set back by hacks and leaks of its unfinished version.

On Monday, 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, pleaded guilty to the Rockstar Games hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

He stole internal tech giant data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished and hugely anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6.

A group of Rockstar workers who were sacked by the company have also been protesting outside its offices, ahead of a tribunal which heard they were penalised for discussing working conditions in a private online forum while working on the game.

They claimed they were punished for being part of a workers' union, but Thomas Cordrey, representing Rockstar, stated employees made disparaging comments about the manufacturer on a semi-public Discord server and shared confidential information.

Tech Now's Laura Cress previews GTA 6 with the game's original creators.

Players were able to download the 212GB game ahead of time, in order to be able to play it as soon as it was made available.

Some had even gone to the lengths of buying a whole new console dedicated to the game.

Broadband providers Virgin Media O2, as well as BT and EE, said internet traffic records had been broken in the days leading up to the UK release.

The BBC has heard from people planning to take time off work - as well as a organization which has given its employees the day off - in order to dedicate time to the game.

He added his partner Clare "has been incredibly understanding, although I suspect she's questioning why our romantic getaway revolves around a PlayStation".

Today, in newly introduced research published on the cover of Science, Google Quantum AI demonstrated that contextuality — a quantum property scientists believe powers certain quantum algorithms — survives at scale on our quantum processor.

In a recent development, what gives quantum computers their unique power? While entanglement usually gets the spotlight, theory suggests that a deeper quantum property called contextuality may power certain quantum algorithms. In simple terms, contextuality means a system’s properties aren’t fixed in advance; what you measure depends on which other compatible measurements you make alongside it.

Sources indicate that until recently, this effect had mostly been shown in small systems of just a few particles. Our paper in Science now demonstrates this at scale on our quantum processor. Using it, our qubits won a well-known coordination game 98.3% of the time, beating the 88.9% classical limit, and outperformed constrained classical strategies in tasks spanning up to 105 qubits.

These tests also serve as a sensitive new method to catch subtle hardware errors, helping pave the way for real-world applications like chemistry and materials science.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Dutch privacy watchdog, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP), has told people not to buy smart glasses, saying they can get things dangerously wrong.
  • It noted in its tests of six glasses available on the Dutch market, the devices advised a user on how to date a child, misread medicine instructions, and claimed to have called an ambulance when they had not.
  • While the AP is advising people not to buy the smart glasses, it stopped short of calling for them to be banned from sale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Dutch privacy watchdog, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP), has told people not to buy smart glasses, saying they can get things dangerously wrong.

It noted in its tests of six glasses available on the Dutch market, the devices advised a user on how to date a child, misread medicine instructions, and claimed to have called an ambulance when they had not.

While the AP is advising people not to buy the smart glasses, it stopped short of calling for them to be banned from sale.

The authority is not revealing which glasses it tested, saying only that prices ranged from under â¬100 (Â£84) to over â¬500 and originated from different continents.

The research follows growing concerns about privacy risks associated with smart glasses, in particular the misuse of the tech to film women without consent, or to record in places where filming is usually prohibited such as healthcare settings.

Meta, a leading seller of the glasses, recently released a version without a camera with some commentators suggesting this was a response to the privacy backlash.

It is unknown if the investigation included Meta's glasses. The AP told the BBC it would not name the products it tested.

The BBC has approached Meta, TCL and HTC - all major manufacturers of smart glasses - for comment.

Previously, these firms have been keen to highlight positive uses of smart glasses.

It has been revealed that meta has highlighted the assistance they can provide to people with visual impairments. Its smart glasses use AI to describe things in the wearer's environment or to read text.

The AP recognises the glasses can be valuable for people who need help to understand their surroundings.

But for these owners, it argues it is particularly crucial that AI is reliable.

AP said in its testing of the unnamed brands, it found the advice given could be wrong.

During a simulated emergency in which CPR resuscitation advice was requested, the AP found one pair of glasses claimed several times an ambulance was on the way - but emergency services had not been contacted.

It mentioned the AI also made child protection errors, with potentially serious consequences.

One pair of glasses gave dating advice to an adult who indicated a romantic interest in a minor.

The glasses also made errors when reading instructions inside medicine packages, as well as with interpreting severe weather warnings.

And the AP was concerned smart glasses could be used to secretly film people, highlighting the ease with which lights, which warn that a device is recording, could be obscured.

It said with some glasses these lights could be covered with tape and they would still work, despite some manufacturers claiming they would not function.

Meanwhile, in some glasses, the AP found serious security flaws which meant someone nearby could connect without permission, view recordings, or even operate the camera remotely.

It warned data recorded by the glasses was often exported outside the EU.

In February, reports revealed outsourced workers were able to view sensitive content recorded on Meta smart glasses.

Meta mentioned at the time such workers might sometimes review content, including video and images, in order to help improve its AI.

It remarked it took the protection of people's data very seriously, and was constantly refining its efforts and tools in that area, and would filter it first to blur faces in images.

The AP investigation was not primarily focused on data protection - instead it was concerned with algorithms and AI.

In the UK Paul Arnold, chief executive of privacy watchdog the Information Commission, who has a severe visual impairment has previously stressed the complexity of the argument, external around smart glasses.

"They can help me and others better understand our surroundings, access information and navigate the world with greater confidence," he wrote in September.

But he noted he had been "shocked and appalled by some of the irresponsible and harmful ways people are using these technologies".

Motorola’s Razr Flex has leaked in full, with the iPhone Duo competitor showing off its wide form factor in two colors, and it looks great.

Following a leaker earlier this morning, SammyGuru has published upcoming images of the Razr Flex, an iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8 competitor that Motorola has been teasing for months now.

It has been revealed that these images show the “Dark Botanical Garden” green and “Coriander” brown with woven and leather-like backplates, two rear-facing cameras, and selfie cameras on both displays. The outer display, said to be 4.97 inches, is wide but very compact, while the inner display is wide in the same way that the iPhone Duo is. The inner panel is expected to be around 7 inches in size.

SammyGuru mentions that the hinge can hold itself half-open and that the price might come in at around $1,799 – though any guesses here are up in the air in the age of RAMageddon.

Motorola Razr Flex is expected to launch in early 2027, with CES in January being a very likely launch timeline for the fresh foldable.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that chinese lab automation company MegaRobo Technologies has raised nearly $200M in a round joined by the Oman Investment Authority and CMB International.
  • China’s MegaRobo Technologies has raised nearly $200M to build labs where AI can run its own experiments, the company confirmed on Thursday.
  • Existing backers Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia and Sinovation Ventures also put in more money.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that chinese lab automation company MegaRobo Technologies has raised nearly $200M in a round joined by the Oman Investment Authority and CMB International. It builds systems that let AI design experiments, run them in robotic labs and learn from the results, and intends to expand across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia.

China’s MegaRobo Technologies has raised nearly $200M to build labs where AI can run its own experiments, the company confirmed on Thursday. The Oman Investment Authority, the country’s sovereign wealth fund, joined the round, along with new investor CMB International.

Existing backers Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia and Sinovation Ventures also put in more money. MegaRobo did not disclose its valuation.

According to recent reports, AI can read papers and predict molecules, but science still needs real tests. MegaRobo links AI models to robots and lab tools. A model can proposal a test, run it and use the results to pick the next one.

“That shift changes AI from a system that interprets the world into one that can help create latest knowledge, materials, processes and products,” stated founder and CEO Daniel Huang.

Recent findings suggest that megaRobo claims it has more than 500 customers, mostly drug makers, biotech firms and research labs. Its Megalaxy Lab lets scientists and AI agents send tests to robot labs, and has served more than 200 of them.

Sources indicate that it has also released Poreva Open, a protein design contest with Tencent Cloud and DNA maker Twist Bioscience. Megalaxy Lab will test more than 10,000 AI-designed proteins in a real lab, to set a shared benchmark built on actual results. Anthropic, for one, had outside labs check Claude’s protein designs in August.

In a recent development, money is pouring into AI drug design. Alphabet’s Isomorphic Labs raised $5B on Tuesday, and Chai Discovery raised $400M in July. In Berlin, Dunia Innovations is building a €280M robotic lab to test what AI designs.

According to recent reports, megaRobo says it has raised about $600M in total, including a $300M Series C backed by Goldman Sachs in 2022. It prepares to expand across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia, and to use the same technology beyond science, much like Jeff Bezos’ physical AI lab.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that its standout spec is a 1.5-inch AMOLED display capable of delivering a staggering 5,500nits of brightness.
  • This should keep it legible in even the harshest sunlight, which every smartwatch user will know can sometimes be a challenge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Honor just debuted its latest smartwatch, the Honor Watch 6 Pro, and it looks like a formidable contender in the wearable space.

Industry observers note that its standout spec is a 1.5-inch AMOLED display capable of delivering a staggering 5,500nits of brightness. This is, as far as I can see per readily available spec information, the brightest smartwatch display on the market right now, beating the 5,000 nits offered by the high-end Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra2 and Garmin fenix 8 Pro.

This should keep it legible in even the harshest sunlight, which every smartwatch user will know can sometimes be a challenge. Despite this brightness, Honor claims that the 515mAh battery will provide up to 18 days of typical usage.

The Honor Watch 6 Pro boasts a 5ATM water resistance (which should make it usable at a depth of up to 50 meters). This is in addition to IP68, IP69, and IP69K dust and water resistance ratings.

You're also getting a wealth of sensors for comprehensive health tracking, including an accelerometer, gyroscope, and optical heart rate sensor, plus dual-frequency GPS for accurate positioning. You can use the watch for contactless payments thanks to its built-in NFC capabilities, too.

All of this comes in an attractive package inspired by premium watchmaking, with a stainless steel front case and nanocrystalline ceramic bezel.

In my eyes, Honor is one of the most exciting smartphone brands right now. Originally a Huawei subsidiary, the manufacturer split off in 2020 and has steadily grown into a serious competitor to the big names like Samsung, Google, Motorola, and Xiaomi. I have tested countless smartphones and tablets, but it's the Honor ones that I keep coming back to because of their high specs and quirky phone designs.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

Honor frequently undercuts its competition with attractive discount coupons and a bombardment of freebies too, and the Honor Watch 6 Pro is no exception. Its price technically starts at £339.99 (that's roughly $450), but the brand is already offering a £100 discount to celebrate the launch, which takes it down to just £229.99 (just above $300).

You also get a free pair of clip-on earbuds, a bonus brown watch strap, and a complimentary 'worry-free' service plan that offers one free repair for screen or liquid damage, as well as an extended warranty service (you can read the full terms of that here).

Recent findings suggest that it's a limited-time offer, but I expect it or similar discounts to return regularly in the coming months and, at this price, the value proposition is excellent on paper. It's going head-to-head with the likes of the Samsung Galaxy Watch8 or Huawei Watch Fit 5 Pro, and beats both on battery life and screen brightness.

I also think the design of the Honor Watch 6 Pro is more attractive, as it looks a lot less like a traditional smartwatch than those two alternatives, but that, of course, comes down to personal preference.

It's not a complete slam dunk, though, as Honor loses to Samsung when it comes to availability, as its products are not officially sold in the US. You also have the matter of Honor's MagicOS software, which tends to be less polished than Samsung's One UI Watch in my experience.

I've reached out to Honor to request a unit to see how it stacks up in the real world, so expect a full review soon.

According to recent reports, but 2013's Grand Theft Auto V was a good-looking, immersive game for its time as well. So we took some time to compare how the games react in similar situations.

In a recent development, what happens when you shoot a window? What happens if you beat up a car? Basically, we tested some of the little things you can do in GTA 5 and GTA 6 between missions out of sheer curiosity.

And if you're just trying to take in the vibes rather than smashing things, you can go to the water's edge and watch the sunset. This is just my opinion, but GTA 6's sunset is gorgeous to watch and is absolutely a vibe.

  • Recent findings suggest that elon Musk has accused Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy of being "untruthful" about Starshield disruptions hampering the nation's ability to defend and fight back against Russia.
  • Recent findings suggest that "From the beginning, I've noted that Starlink is a civilian system," Musk told interviewer Andrew Ross Sorkin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

He stated that Ukraine is trying to use SpaceX’s consumer Starlink service for military purposes.

Recent findings suggest that elon Musk has accused Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy of being "untruthful" about Starshield disruptions hampering the nation's ability to defend and fight back against Russia. The SpaceX CEO told The New York Times' DealBook Summit that Ukraine is actually trying to use the tech giant's consumer Starlink service, not Starshield, for military purposes.

Recent findings suggest that "From the beginning, I've noted that Starlink is a civilian system," Musk told interviewer Andrew Ross Sorkin. "It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people. If you want to do that, you need to use Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government. But do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions.".

Musk's comments come amid a lengthy disruption to Starshield in Ukraine. Last month, Zelenskyy posted on X that speed limits on Starshield were imposed along the war's entire front line and in Russian territory, saying any terminal moving faster than 161 km/h (100 mph) would lose its connection to the satellite network. "Unfortunately, this is helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine," Zelenskyy mentioned at the time. "We are trying to establish all the circumstances with the American side.".

It has been revealed that sorkin reminded Musk that Zelenskyy referred to the system being slowed down as Starshield and not Starlink. "That's false... [Zelenskyy is] not always truthful,"  Musk replied. "What he is actually saying is he wants to use Starlink for offensive military operations.".

The last time Starshield was slowed on October 14, SpaceX and The White House blamed each other for throttling speeds, but nothing was ever confirmed. Citing US officials, Reuters had reported that the order came from inside the White House. Later on, though, The Wall Street Journal's sources stated  that Musk himself ordered the slowdown.

Later in October, Ukraine pushed back against allegations that it had misused Starlink for offensive attacks. An official said that pre-existing restrictions on the systems would have made it "physically impossible" for Ukraine to use Starlink to strike in Russian territory as Musk described.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Theraguns are the gold standard for massage guns; the brand name has come to be synonymous with the entire product category, much like “Kleenex” is for tissues.
  • I haven't yet tried every product in the Therabody lineup (I’m getting there), but I've put most to the test and am ready to recommend my favorites.
  • Industry observers note that need more gift ideas for the active person in your life?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Theraguns are the gold standard for massage guns; the brand name has come to be synonymous with the entire product category, much like “Kleenex” is for tissues. But Therabody, the innovative company behind Theragun, offers more than relief for sore muscles and pain. It now sells a broad repertoire of wellness gadgets aimed at alleviating ailments like eye strain, menstrual cramps, and skin puffiness (to name a few). So whether you’re shopping for a fitness lover or someone who could use a little self-care, there’s likely a Therabody gadget worth wrapping up.

I haven't yet tried every product in the Therabody lineup (I’m getting there), but I've put most to the test and am ready to recommend my favorites. Plus, most are FSA/HSA-eligible and designed with USB-C charging capability.

Industry observers note that need more gift ideas for the active person in your life? Check out our guides to the Best Massage Guns, Best Massagers, and Best Compression Boots.

Updated November 2026: I’ve added the Theragun Prime (6th Gen) and removed discontinued products. I also confirmed up-to-date links and prices.

Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.

If you’re looking for a professional-grade massage device, the Theragun Pro Plus is one of the most advanced percussive guns on the market, incorporating vibrations, heat, and near-infrared LED therapies for an all-in-one recovery tool. It also offers cold therapy, but you'll have to purchase an additional attachment for $100 to make use of that capability—a steep add-on for what is already a splurge. After testing the attachment myself, I don't think it justifies the cost unless you are sure you'd regularly use the contrast therapy.

Priced at $650, this is the most expensive Theragun, so I'd recommend it to athletes or those who are dealing with chronic muscle pain and want the LED therapy. For casual users, some of the features might feel like overkill. For example, there's a built-in biometric sensor for heart rate tracking that I have barely used. I do, though, appreciate the OLED screen, which displays a force meter, so you can see exactly how much pressure you're applying. It's a useful function if you need a nudge to apply more pressure or a reminder to ease up.

Recent findings suggest that the Theragun Prime (6th Gen) hits the sweet spot between the elite Pro Plus and the budget-friendly Relief. It’s still a premium percussive massage gun, with five speed settings, two attachments (a dampener and standard ball), and up to 120 minutes of battery life. You won’t get extras like heated or near-infrared LED therapy, or compatibility with Therabody’s cold and vibration attachments, but you will enjoy top-notch durability. It’s the only Theragun in the lineup rated to withstand drops from up to 10 feet, making it an excellent gift for the accident-prone person in your life.

The Theragun Relief, introduced in 2023, remains the cheapest Theragun—priced even lower than the Mini Plus. For the price tag, you’re sacrificing some of the premium features, like the LCD screen and Bluetooth connectivity to the Therabody app for device control. But you can still follow guided routines on the app, and the simple one-button control is refreshingly simple to use.

The Relief comes with three head attachments and has three speed settings, which is a step down from models that offer a standard five speeds and four or more attachments. Still, the Relief is less than half the weight of the Pro Plus, and it's equipped with the essentials, which is more than enough for the average person.

The original Theragun Mini is still a solid portable device—and it's $60 less—but the Mini Plus feels like a shrunken version of the elite Pro Plus. The ergonomic triangular design lets me target trigger points and muscle groups like my hamstrings and calves with more pressure control (though, admittedly, that same shape makes it awkward to use on my lower back). Thoughtful details, like a travel lock to prevent it from powering on and a compact carrying pouch, make it easy to carry on commutes and flights.

Most notably, it brings heated percussive therapy to a travel-friendly device. The heat therapy is easily my favorite feature on the Pro Plus. The Mini Plus is also compatible with Therabody's Vibration Plus and Cold Plus attachments (both sold separately).

Note: Some customers have reported charging concerns, saying their units wouldn't power up, but I haven't run into any battery problems in my two weeks of testing. I'll patch this review if anything shifts with long-term use.

In a recent development, the JetBoots Pro Plus are full-length, wireless boots that combine pneumatic compression with vibration therapy and infrared LED light. Everything is controlled from a built-in LCD screen and control panel on the lead boot, and connectivity is effortless, automatically linking when powered on.

Eight preset programs target legs, knees, and joints, but you can manually adjust pressure, intensity, and the session length. Sessions can run from 10 to 60 minutes in five-minute increments, with compression adjustable between 20 and 100 millimeters of mercury (mmHg)—a standard unit of measurement for pressure. Vibration offers three intensity levels (low, medium, and high), and the infrared LED setting is a simple on or off, with an automatic shutoff after 45 minutes.

Industry observers note that inside the boots, a nonporous proprietary material reduces moisture and microbial buildup, and after months of testing, I haven't noticed any lingering odors. These are best suited for athletes, frequent travelers, or anyone managing circulation-related conditions. Conveniently for those aforementioned jet-setters, the JetBoots Pro Plus are TSA-approved for carry-on travel; just keep in mind that they're pretty hefty.

According to recent reports, I enjoyed the original TheraFace Mask, but the upgraded TheraFace Mask Glo feels like the smarter purchase. It's easier to find (Therabody seems to be phasing out the original), costs $270 less, and is slightly lighter at 1.13 pounds versus the OG's 1.27 pounds. While the Glo has fewer LED bulbs—504 compared to 648—the difference doesn't translate to a lesser treatment. You get the same red, infrared, and blue light wavelengths, plus the signature vibration therapy that made the first-generation mask stand out.

The vibrations are now integrated into the adjustable straps rather than the mask itself. They're usually distracting, occasionally even headache-inducing, depending on my mood. I usually skip the vibration setting altogether to make this component less irritating. Even without it, the Glo remains competitively priced among high-end LED masks.

It has been revealed that treatment sessions range from four to 12 minutes, and the removable eye shields are thoughtful, but I prefer taking them off to extend the light coverage to my under-eye area. I very much appreciate the cordless design, but I do miss the display stand that came with the original. I often end up storing it back in its box, which makes me less inclined to reach for it. If you, too, deal with this issue, you might consider buying a travel case for $80.

I challenge you to stay awake through a full session with the SmartGoggles 2.0. I’ve been testing them for months, and more often than not, I conk out while wearing them. The combination of gentle heat, vibration, and massage therapy across my forehead, eyebrows, and temples relaxes my facial tension within minutes. I love wearing them when I have a headache from staring at screens all day, and while I don’t struggle with regular migraines, I can see them being a soothing blackout remedy in a quiet, dark room.

Former reviewer Medea Giordano loved the first model, and this upgrade improves the fit with contoured padding that feels similar to Therabody’s SleepMask. You still get three preset modes: Focus, Sleep, and SmartRelax. That last option uses biometric feedback to adjust vibration patterns based on your heart rate. It also syncs with the Therabody app, letting you tweak the vibration and heat intensities or incorporate sound therapy. Note, though, if you’re a side-sleeper, you’ll have to shift around, as these are most comfortable while lying flat on your back.

Sources indicate that I’ve tested several sleep masks, and the TheraFace SleepMask is among my favorites. Many claim to be 100 percent blackout, but this one leaves me feeling totally disoriented when I wake up, with no idea what dimension I'm in—just how I like it. The contoured padding feels plush, and the adjustable strap keeps the mask in place without tugging at my hair, even when I shift around at night. It comes with a carrying case, so I always pack it for travel.

Recent findings suggest that the selling point is that this mask uses vibrations—three pattern presets (Pulse, Wave, Constant)—designed to nudge your brain into deeper rest. I struggle with staying asleep, but when I wake up in the middle of the night, I just tap the button to start a 15-minute session, and it usually lulls me back to sleep. That said, the vibrations are almost too gentle; you barely feel them, but you can absolutely hear them. It's not as soothing as a white noise machine, so if you're a light sleeper, this might be a deal-breaker.

According to recent reports, the TheraFace Depuffing Wand has become a staple in my travel bag. It delivers both hot and cold therapy to help reduce puffiness, improve circulation, and enhance product absorption before completing your skin care routine. It’s TSA-friendly—zero awkward bag checks and counting—and ideal for tackling under-eye bags after a long flight or night. The curved applicator reaches every contour of my face, and the precision tip is great for trickier spots like under my eyes. It’s intended to be used on clean, dry skin, so I hold the opposite side of my face to prevent tugging.

According to recent reports, the wand comes with three preset temperature levels that feel gentle but effective. While the cold function isn’t as icy as a roller fresh from the freezer, it’s consistent throughout a six-minute session and doesn’t drip. Plus, this one won’t crack if you forget to take it out of the freezer (RIP to two of my traditional rollers). An indicator light flashes at three minutes to remind you to switch sides, but this notification is easy to miss if you’re not looking straight into a mirror.

Cupping is an ancient healing technique that uses suction to provide muscle relief. Therabody's version combines suction, heat, and vibration therapy for localized recovery. With three levels of suction (30, 40, and 50 kilopascals, or kPa), three heat intensities (41, 43, and 45 degrees Celsius), and three vibration modes (low, high, and wave), I appreciate how you can customize the intensity of your session. The TheraCup is also programmed with an auto-shutoff after three minutes—so you don’t overdo any area—and built-in safety sensors that will cut off the pressure if it exceeds 60 kPa.

According to recent reports, theraFace Mask for $650: The TheraFace Mask is a cordless, hands-free light-therapy device that uses three wavelengths (red, infrared, and blue) to tackle different skin care goals. As a distinguishing feature from its competitors, the TheraFace Mask includes a built-in vibration therapy mode that massages pressure points around the eyes, brow line, and scalp for some added stress relief. It comes with removable eye shields and a sleek display stand, which makes it easy to store on your nightstand.

JetBoots Prime for $550: Compared to the JetBoots Pro Plus, the JetBoots Prime is simple to use: You get four pressure levels (25, 50, 75, and 100 mmHg) and three durations (20, 40, or 60 minutes), all adjustable throughout your session through a built-in control panel. Th boots are wireless with a 180-minute battery life and can even be used while charging. Plus, they fold down into the included drawstring bag, making them portable and fuss-free to stow away.

In a recent development, waveRoller for $180: Foam rollers are great for improving range of motion, increasing blood flow, and reducing muscle tension. You can buy a decent foam roller for significantly less, but with the WaveRoller, you get Therabody app integration for a personalized experience and five vibration frequencies. Designed for full-body use, it works best for warm-ups and post-workout recovery.

Theragun Mini (3rd Generation) for $220: I recommend the Mini if you’re upcoming to percussive therapy or need something packable for travel. It's the smallest and lightest Theragun, with three attachments (standard ball, dampener, and thumb) and a soft-zip case that fits into a tote, gym bag, or carry-on.

Theragun Sense for $300: The Theragun Sense is slightly smaller (and lighter) than the Pro Plus, and it’s also impressively quiet. Some settings are almost silent, allowing for a discreet recovery session at any time of day without worrying about bothering your housemates. It has the same LCD screen and breathwork features as the Pro Plus, too. The main difference here is that it's compatible with fewer attachments, but four heads are still more than enough for many active individuals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that AI has taken over everything in the past few years, with AI features bombarding virtually every app or service available. If you’ve ever wanted to just turn off AI features, Canva proves that it could be a simple toggle, if companies actually wanted to give you a choice.

Canva today revealed “AI Controls,” a upcoming toggle that completely turns off generative AI features within the editing app.

Generative AI can be quite helpful in working on posters, editing images, and more, but it’s not everyone’s preference. Canva puts this well:.

For some people, AI is the most exciting creative tool in a generation, while others prefer bringing their ideas to life without it. We believe the future of creativity should give everyone the freedom to choose their own path, whether that’s creating with AI, without it, or somewhere in between.

In a recent development, to give its customers the choice, Canva’s Permissions menu now has a simple toggle for “Enable Generative AI features.” Toggling it off disables features such as Magic Write and Magic Edit. There’s also an option to limit how much AI-generated imagery appears in the Canva library.

Put simply, this is great to see.

In a recent development, AI has its place, but everyone should have a choice like this, especially when it comes to apps and services used for artistry in the same vein as Canva. Yet, the tech industry continues to go in the opposite direction, shoving AI into every corner whether it’s actually useful or not. Canva proves, though, that it doesn’t have to be that way.
